newsitem.title: SPAIN: BoS sold marks for pesetas at 84.70 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: BoS sold marks for pesetas at 84.70 - dealers.

text.p: Traders said on Friday they had seen the Bank of Spain selling marks for pesetas at 84.70, after the Spanish currency weakened in morning trade.
"The central bank has been selling marks and buying pesetas at 84.70 just to hold that barrier," said one Madrid trader.
The Bank of Spain declined as a matter of policy to comment.
By 1200 GMT, the peseta was trading at 84.65/67 per mark, after touching 84.71 and compared with 84.50/53 late on Thursday.
Traders pointed out that 84.70 was the level at which the central bank had been buying pesetas on Wednesday.
But traders suspected that any intervention would have involved small quantities.
Some traders said, however, that the mark would try to break the 84.70 level and head for 85.00 per mark.
A failure to break 84.70 could push the market back toward 84.40.
"Last time the Bank of Spain was buying pesetas at this level the market corrected back to 84.40 per mark," said one trader.
